name: Tibia
description: Proximal tibia: concave medial and flatter lateral plateaus separated by the intercondylar eminence, with the ACL footprint in front of it, the PCL footprint behind, the tuberosity anteriorly and Gerdy's tubercle anterolaterally. Adult epiphyseal marrow is fatty and a physeal scar often persists.

normal_values.tt_tg_distance: under 20 mm on CT (20 mm or more is pathologic); MRI reads about 2–4 mm lower

variants_pitfalls: Red marrow follows the femoral rules (patchy, isointense to or brighter than muscle on T1, epiphysis spared) but is less common here; darker than muscle needs workup.
The physeal scar slopes down anteriorly into the tuberosity and is not a fracture; focal edema around a closing physis in adolescents is physiologic.
Cruciate footprint cysts (about 1% of knee MRIs): well-defined fluid cysts beneath the ACL or PCL attachment, often with ACL mucoid degeneration; usually incidental.

Where injury hides: edema at the posterior lip of the medial plateau came with an ACL tear in every case and a peripheral medial posterior horn or meniscocapsular tear in 96% of one series. Posterolateral plateau plus lateral condyle edema is the pivot-shift pattern.
